summary: Round 3 genuinely fixes the three issues it claims to fix (the user-writable _cgroup_path config-file indirection is removed in favor of a hardcoded /proc/self/cgroup read with a narrow, disclosed test-only env-var seam; the leading '+' force-push marker is now stripped before comparison; every positional refspec is now checked instead of just the first), and all of this is backed by real regression tests that source the actual shipped snippet rather than a reimplementation. However, live reproduction against the actual shipped git wrapper found a complete, undisclosed bypass of the entire git-push protection: the wrapper only intercepts a push when the literal first argument is 'push' ($1 = "push"), but git accepts standard global options before the subcommand name (-C <path>, -c <key>=<value>, --git-dir=, --work-tree=, --no-pager, etc.). Running 'git -C . push origin master' or 'git -c user.name=x push origin master' shifts $1 away from 'push', so the guard's detection never fires and the command falls straight through to 'exec "$_real_git" "$@"' unblocked -- verified live against the fixture harness (fake git logged REAL_GIT_CALLED with the push intact, exit 0, no BLOCKED message). This is the same class of real, non-obscure, easily-reproduced bypass this task's own round-2/round-3 methodology was built to hunt for, yet it was not found, tested, or disclosed in known_limitations. Given this is a security-relevant write-gate whose entire purpose is closing exactly this kind of gap, and the bypass fully defeats protection against pushing to a protected branch with an ordinary git invocation, this should not be merged as-is.
issues: Live-reproduced: 'git -C . push origin master' and 'git -c user.name=x push origin master' completely bypass the write-gate (git wrapper's dispatch only checks literal $1 = "push"; any git global option before the subcommand, e.g. -C, -c, --git-dir=, --work-tree=, --no-pager, shifts the subcommand out of $1 and the command execs the real git unblocked). Needs a round 4 fix that scans argv for the 'push' token while correctly skipping global-option arguments (including those, like -C and -c, that consume a following value), not just checking $1.

This exact gap is undisclosed in the diff's known_limitations section, despite the file's stated standard of disclosing every residual bypass found -- the round-3 write-up should either fix this or explicitly document it alongside the absolute-path-invocation and command -p limitations already listed.
No .github/workflows/** files are touched by this diff, so the hard workflow-scope rule in SUPERBOSS_DISPATCH_PROMPT.md does not apply here.
